comparator.name: Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum totals 180 ECTS. The first two years each contain 60 ECTS combining entrepreneurship, innovation, business foundations, quantitative methods and four successive Entrepreneurship in Action projects. Year 3 contains a 30-ECTS mobility/minor/internship window, Philosophy for Business, a 12-ECTS graduation project, one 6-ECTS specialisation choice and one 6-ECTS elective. Zero-credit GROW activity is excluded. The specialisation and elective components remain genuine choices rather than being populated with assumed courses.
components: Entrepreneurship in Action 1: Forming an Effective Team
Entrepreneurship in Action 2: Reaching Problem-Solution Fit
Entrepreneurship in Action 3: Developing a Business Model
Entrepreneurship in Action 4: Developing a Business Plan
Choice among exchange, Economics and Management minors, another Tilburg minor, or a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective.
Choice among Advanced Startup Entrepreneurship, Advanced Corporate Entrepreneurship, and Advanced Impact Entrepreneurship.
Choice among Making Deals, Joining the Family Business, International Entrepreneurship, and Investment Decisions.

core: Entrepreneurship, venture creation, entrepreneurial mindset and business innovation
Business foundations, accounting, finance, economics and law
Market opportunities, entrepreneurial marketing, business models and problem-solution fit
Quantitative methods, programming and data-driven decisions
Leadership, ethics, teams, creative problem-solving and deal-making
Evidence-based entrepreneurial practice, research, pitching and graduation work
adjacent: Corporate entrepreneurship, digital innovation and change inside organisations
Impact entrepreneurship and sustainable, socially valuable ventures
questions: How can an entrepreneur identify an opportunity, test problem-solution fit and build a viable business model?
How can entrepreneurial thinking and digital tools drive innovation inside an existing organisation?
How can ventures create economic value while producing social or environmental impact?

alternatives.label: Entrepreneurial ventures & business innovation
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible entrepreneurship programme combining venture creation, business-model development, marketing, finance, economics, leadership, research and data-informed decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres opportunity recognition, venture development, business models, marketing, finance, leadership and evidence-based decisions; the label makes the specialist entrepreneurial organising logic explicit.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, leadership and communication foundations precede advanced strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, econometrics, market research and international governance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Corporate entrepreneurship, digital innovation & strategy
alternatives.concept: A corporate-entrepreneurship route organised around strategic change, analytics, digital systems and innovation inside established organisations, combining programming, AI and data with economics, finance, marketing and entrepreneurship.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines business and entrepreneurship with programming, databases, data science, machine learning and algorithmic decision tools.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces substantial leadership, finance, qualitative-research and entrepreneurship content with programming, databases, linear algebra, probability, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics. Ten of the 24 courses differ, and digital analytics becomes the programme's organising logic.
progression: Business, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced strategy, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, international business and market research. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and deep learning; programming precedes algorithms. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Impact entrepreneurship & sustainable ventures
alternatives.concept: An impact-entrepreneurship route combining venture development, management, economics, marketing, leadership and research with climate, circular economy, environmental governance and ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum joins business, entrepreneurship and leadership to a sustained sequence in sustainability, circular economy, governance and ethics.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and digital routes, this curriculum gives sustained weight to climate, circular economy, sustainability science, ecological innovation, environmental governance, remediation and renewable-system design. Ten courses differ from the closest programme and fourteen from the digital route, making responsible and sustainable entrepreneurship the governing academic direction.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

candidates.label: Corporate entrepreneurship, digital innovation and strategic change

selection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers entrepreneurship, innovation and venture development. Corporate entrepreneurship/digital innovation and impact entrepreneurship/sustainable ventures each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantially distinct additional programmes. Three alternatives are included, the maximum.

notes.text: Tilburg requires four successive Entrepreneurship in Action projects, dedicated entrepreneurship contexts, a 12-ECTS graduation project and a chosen advanced specialisation. UCR can build coherent venture, corporate-innovation and impact-enterprise pathways but does not reproduce that complete specialist practice sequence.
